title: Bounded constructible complexes with field coefficients form a triangulated subcategory
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme and $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$. The full subcategory
$\Dbc(X,\Lambda)\subseteq D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ contains $0$, is closed under
isomorphisms and under the shifts $[\pm1]$, and if two vertices of a distinguished triangle
lie in $\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ then so does the third. Hence it is a triangulated subcategory, and
it is thick.

proof.text: For either coefficient ring use det-lem-coefficient-heart-closure on X, with IsNoetherian constructed from the existing locally Noetherian and compact hypotheses. Set P to IsConstantModelConstructible. Install its kernel, cokernel and extension closure. The closure theorem supplies an abelian structure on its full subcategory. Its zero object maps to an ambient zero object under the full inclusion, since a full functor preserves zero morphisms. This supplies P.ContainsZero. Obtain isomorphism closure from the first clause of det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude. These constructions also apply on the empty scheme.

Apply lem-sbc-cohomology-in-weak-serre-subcategory to P. Its proved generic argument uses the five-term exact cohomology sequence, kernel/cokernel closure and extension closure, exactly the unit cone argument. Intersect its triangulated homology property with canonical boundedness. Both properties are invariant under isomorphisms. Their intersection is definitionally constantModelBoundedConstructible, and the object-property intersection instances supply repleteness and IsTriangulated.

For a retract M of N with inclusion i and retraction r, construct the kernel fork of 1 - r followed by i, with kernel inclusion i. A map g annihilating this endomorphism satisfies g = g r i; its unique lift is g r. Thus any class closed under kernels is stable under retracts between its objects. Apply this to every cohomology retract. For boundedness choose bounds a,b for N using exists_homologyConcentratedIn_iff_bounded; homologyConcentratedIn a b is stable under retracts, so the same bounds hold for M. This proves thickness.

Specialize the preceding construction to continuousMapRingSheaf E for each finite intermediate field, using E.2 for finite dimensionality, and to padicAlgClCondensedRing. The underlying abelian sheaves and ring-object structures are definitionally the coefficient objects in the statement, so the two applications assemble the required conjunction.
